note: Lakelawn Estate is drawn from the 1974 Bushnell East quadrangle: aerial photographs 1973, field check 1974. The curved streets and the pond are not on the 1944 Avon sheet. The assessor dates the houses from 1963 to 1979. The plat recording date is not in the online county record. Streets the 1918 and 1944 sheets already draw are on the earlier stops.

update.name: Martin-Hollis Funeral Home
update.notes: photo from Mark, 771 N. Crafford St., 2010. The name Martin-Hollis is the one on dodsworthfh.com/location/bushnell and on legacy.com. A funeral-home directory dates that partnership to 1967, so the name is on the card from the 1970 stop and is not painted on the wall. The 2010 photograph does not show the words on the facade.

update.name: Something Special

facade.photoDate: 2010. The sign is not drawn before the 1970 stop.
facade.photoSource: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010

update.sourceMap: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010
update.notes: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010. The Hurst-corner front of the 400 block is the wide cream brick building in that photograph: six upstairs windows filled with red-brown panels under cream hoods, a cornice with dentils and brackets, and a central pediment with a finial. The ground floor is glass, with a brown band reading Something Special and a red-and-white striped canopy at the right end. Something Special is the 2010 sign. It is not drawn before 1970. The earlier years keep the red brick bank front.

facade.photoSource: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010

update.notes: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010. The front next to the Hurst corner is the green-painted brick building: three upstairs windows under white arched hoods, a corbelled cornice, a shingled pent roof, and a low brick base. No name is printed on this front. The 1907 iron storefront and canvas awning stay through 1960.

facade.photoSource: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010

update.notes: photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010. The third front north of the Hurst corner is painted gray-white, with two arched hoods upstairs and a later glass storefront. No name on that front was read. The earlier frame storefront stays through 1960.
